title: Arrays Have Fixed Sizes
goal: Understand fixed-size array types and repetition syntax.

sections.text: An array in Rust holds a fixed number of elements of the same type. The length is written directly in the type signature.

sections.caption: [i32; 3] is an array of three 32-bit integers.

sections.text: Because length is part of the type, `[i32; 3]` and `[i32; 4]` are completely different types. You cannot pass a four-element array to a function expecting three.

sections.caption: [value; count] repeats a single initial value.

sections.text: Arrays live on the stack and cannot change size. Dynamic lists use `Vec`, which is covered in a later deck.

explanation: Understand fixed-size array types and repetition syntax.
